title: Lisse heart closure for all-continuous algebraic-closure coefficients
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers] with its extended $\ell$-adic norm topology, and the commutative condensed ring $\Lambda(P)=C(P,\Omega)$ of all continuous functions on profinite sets [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. There is no finite-subextension restriction. On each scheme $T$ put $R_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and use internal module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] whose underlying topological space is Noetherian, meaning that every descending chain of closed subsets stabilizes. An $R_T$-module is lisse if on a pro-etale cover it is a finite direct sum $R_T^r$, with $r=0$ allowed [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. Having a finite constant local model [sk-def-sfb-constructible], namely being pro-etale locally $R_T\otimes_{\underline\Omega}\underline V$ for a finitely presented scalar $\Omega$-module $V$, is equivalent to being lisse. The full class of lisse $R_T$-modules contains zero and is closed under isomorphisms, kernels and cokernels of morphisms between its objects, and extensions: for every morphism $u:L\to M$ of lisse modules, $\ker u$ and $\operatorname{coker}u$, computed in the ambient module category, are lisse; for every short exact sequence $0\to L\to E\to M\to0$ with lisse ends, $E$ is lisse. This holds in particular on every locally closed subscheme of a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and does not require choosing a finite coefficient field.

proof.text: The scalar ring is $\Lambda(*)=\Omega$: a continuous function from a point is its value. A finitely presented $\Omega$-module $V$ has a finite basis by [lem-sfb-scalar-finite-free-resolutions], so $V\cong\Omega^r$. Extension of this scalar isomorphism gives $R_U\otimes_{\underline\Omega}\underline V\cong R_U^r$ on each member of the cover. Conversely $\Omega^r$ is finitely presented and gives the local model for $R_U^r$. Thus the finite constant local models of [sk-def-sfb-constructible] are exactly the lisse modules of [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module], including rank zero. The finite constant local model comparison and its finite-free scalar-extension isomorphism [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model] keep the same cover in both directions.

source.place: Definition 3.3 and stable-subcategory observation, Definition 6.1 and Theorem 6.2(2), pp. 7 and 16-17

proof.text: Every ideal of the field Ω is projective. Specialize the proved general result [lem-sfb-semihereditary-topological-coefficients-admissible] to Ω: it gives regular coherence, finite projective resolutions and flat continuous-function sections, hence t-admissibility for the canonical all-continuous condensed ring. The two continuous coefficient presentations agree definitionally, including the canonical monoid structure. This uses neither completeness nor restriction to finite subextensions. A Noetherian space has finitely many irreducible components by [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components], hence Zariski locally finite components (take the whole space around every point).

proof.text: Apply [lem-zl-t-admissible-dualizable-truncations] directly in the internal module derived category. Its heart equivalence identifies a module in degree zero as dualizable exactly when it has scalar local models. The existing finite constant local model comparison [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model] identifies these with the statement's finite constant local models, and step 1 identifies them with lisse modules. The comparison to ordinary sheaf modules is already internal to the cited general theorem; no further equivalence is required here.

source.place: Definition 3.3 and stable-subcategory observation, Definition 6.1 and Theorem 6.2(2), pp. 7 and 16-17

proof.text: The stable-subcategory assertion of [lem-zl-condensed-dualizable-local-perfect-models] gives a triangulated property P of dualizable complexes, closed under isomorphisms. The standard degree-zero inclusion is fully faithful and has essential image the ambient standard heart. For a map of lisse modules form a distinguished cone Z, which belongs to P. Apply [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles]: its ambient kernel K has K[1] isomorphic to the standard truncation tau_{<=-1} Z, while its ambient cokernel Q is isomorphic to tau_{>=0} Z. Truncation stability from [lem-zl-t-admissible-dualizable-truncations], followed by shift and isomorphism stability, puts K[0] and Q[0] in P. Thus both are lisse by step 3. Uniqueness of limiting kernel forks and colimiting cokernel coforks proves closure for every ambient choice. The zero complex belongs to P, degree-zero inclusion preserves zero, and isomorphisms preserve P, giving the zero and isomorphism clauses.

source.place: Definition 3.3 and stable-subcategory observation, Definition 6.1 and Theorem 6.2(2), pp. 7 and 16-17

proof.text: For an ambient short exact sequence 0 → L → E → M → 0 with lisse ends, the degree-zero derived inclusion gives its distinguished triangle by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle]. The triangulated dualizable class of [lem-zl-t-admissible-dualizable-truncations] is closed under extensions: rotating once and applying cone closure is the standard IsTriangulatedClosed₂ operation. The end objects lie in that class by step 3, so the arbitrary middle object E[0] does too. Apply the degree-zero heart criterion and step 1 to conclude that E is lisse.

source.place: Definition 3.3 and stable-subcategory observation, Definition 6.1 and Theorem 6.2(2), pp. 7 and 16-17

proof.text: Every subspace $Y$ of a Noetherian topological space $X$ is Noetherian: for descending closed subsets $F_n$ of $Y$, the closures $\overline{F_n}^{\,X}$ form a descending closed chain in $X$ and stabilize; intersecting with $Y$ gives back $F_n$ and hence stabilization. The topology of a locally closed subscheme is its subspace topology. The underlying space of the Noetherian scheme $X$ of the final clause is Noetherian: by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal] the members of a descending chain of closed subsets have a minimal member, after which the chain is constant. Thus each locally closed subscheme of $X$ satisfies the hypothesis on $T$, and steps 1-5 apply to it with the same all-continuous coefficient ring. This also includes the empty scheme.
